cognate: OIr. bó = Gk βοῦς (*gʷōu-); OIr. míl = Gk μῆλον (*mēlo-, also MW mil, Arm. mal)
drift_or_renewal: míl has widened from 'small livestock' to 'animal' in Irish generally, but here the beasts are milked (no-mbligtis ... blechta), i.e. milch small stock, the Greek sense of μῆλα
shared_syntax: coordinated pair of the two livestock nouns, 'cattle and small stock' (Ir. cech bó ocus cech míl; Gk μῆλα καὶ (εἰλίποδας ἕλικας) βοῦς), a two-member merism for the whole herd
context: herd animals in a pastoral setting: in Longes mac nUislenn every cow and beast that heard the sons of Uisliu's song yielded two thirds more milk; in Homer/Hesiod the herdsmen's flocks (shield scene), sacrificial animals, livestock to be tended. Both use the pair as 'all the livestock'. Caveat: Only one Irish attestation (Longes mac nUislenn and its copies) in the CELT layer; no Welsh or Armenian parallel found (no kov+mal in DMHP). Greek pair is formulaic. A 'cow and other beast' pairing could arise independently; the cognate second slot plus the milking context is what makes it worth recording. Etymology of míl/μῆλον recalled.
